findings.title: Admin member routes supply :id but controller requires :group_id
findings.body: In config/routes.rb the lines `delete "members"` and `put "members"` are declared directly inside `resources :groups` so Rails makes them member routes like /admin/groups/:id/members. The actions in app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb do `Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i)` for both add_members and remove_member. That required param will never be present, so every call raises ActionController::ParameterMissing and member add/remove is broken.

findings.title: Public members endpoint accepts unbounded limit/offset
findings.body: GroupsController#members does `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` then `limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no clamping, maximum, or non-negative check. An attacker can request limit=1000000 or negative values to force a huge DB load/serialization or an exception, causing DoS or 500s. The endpoint needs a cap such as 200 and to force offset >= 0.

findings.title: totalPages off-by-one breaks last-page detection
findings.body: totalPages is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` in app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100/50) this yields 3 instead of 2, so showingLast never becomes true at the right time, the pager shows a phantom page, and the next action can set offset == user_count which returns an empty page.

findings.title: add_members does not trim usernames
findings.body: Admin::GroupsController#add_members does `usernames.split(",").each` then `User.find_by_username(username)` with no strip. The user-selector sends comma+space separated names like "alice, bob", so the second lookup becomes " bob" and silently fails, so only the first user is added and the admin gets a success response with missing members.

findings.title: remove_member deletes by raw integer id
findings.body: Admin::GroupsController#remove_member does `group.users.delete(user_id)` where user_id is an Integer from params. Has-many-through collection#delete expects model instances and bypasses association callbacks/destroy logic; passing an id may no-op, raise, or leave the join record inconsistent. It should load the User and call group.remove(user) or delete the GroupUser record.
